paper_metadata.title: Corrosion and Carburization Behaviour of Ni-Cr-Mo-Nb Superalloys in a High Temperature Supercritical-CO2 Environment
paper_metadata.journal: Proceedings of the 9th International Symposium on Superalloy 718 & Derivatives: Energy, Aerospace, and Industrial Applications, The Minerals, Metals & Materials Series

evidence.quote: Two Ni-Cr-Mo-Nb superalloys (Alloy 625 and Alloy 718) were corroded in high temperature supercritical-CO2 (S-CO2) at 700 °C (20 MPa) for 500 h

Solid-solution strengthened Ni-base superalloy 625 and precipitate-hardened Ni-base superalloy 718 were used in this study. Their chemical compositions were analyzed by inductively coupled plasma (ICP) spectroscopy and are listed in Table 1.

phases_and_microstructures.name: Cr2O3
phases_and_microstructures.material_state: exposed to S-CO2 at 700 °C (20 MPa) for 500 h

evidence.quote: For Alloy 625, a continuous chromia layer (∼1 μm thickness) was formed on the surface (Fig. 5)

phases_and_microstructures.name: Ni3(Nb, Mo)
phases_and_microstructures.material_state: exposed to S-CO2 at 700 °C (20 MPa) for 500 h

evidence.quote: an enrichment of Nb and Mo was found adjacent to the oxide/metal interface, having rod-like morphology. Diffraction pattern analysis in this region confirmed it to be δ-phase [Ni3(Nb, Mo)] (Fig. 5c).

phases_and_microstructures.name: Cr2O3
phases_and_microstructures.material_state: exposed to S-CO2 at 700 °C (20 MPa) for 500 h

evidence.quote: In the case of Alloy 718 (Fig. 3c), large nodular oxide islands can be observed, with rest of the area being a continuous oxide similar in morphology to that formed on Alloy 625.

phases_and_microstructures.name: Fe3O4
phases_and_microstructures.material_state: exposed to S-CO2 at 700 °C (20 MPa) for 500 h

evidence.quote: Oxide peaks detected on Alloy 718 were identified to be Fe3O4, NiO and chromia.

phases_and_microstructures.name: NiO
phases_and_microstructures.material_state: exposed to S-CO2 at 700 °C (20 MPa) for 500 h

evidence.quote: Oxide peaks detected on Alloy 718 were identified to be Fe3O4, NiO and chromia.

phases_and_microstructures.name: Ni3(Nb, Mo)
phases_and_microstructures.material_state: exposed to S-CO2 at 700 °C (20 MPa) for 500 h

evidence.quote: some Nb and Mo enriched regions can be seen under the oxide layer. Ni is seen to be also slightly enriched in these regions, and thus, these areas can also be corresponded to oxidation-induced δ-phase [Ni3(Nb, Mo)], as also detected by XRD analysis.

phases_and_microstructures.name: amorphous C layer
phases_and_microstructures.material_state: exposed to S-CO2 at 700 °C (20 MPa) for 500 h

evidence.quote: for Alloy 718, EDS line scan at the oxide/matrix interface revealed enrichment of C below chromia (Fig. 7b). This area could be identified as an amorphous C layer by HRTEM and diffraction pattern analysis (Fig. 7c)

phases_and_microstructures.name: nodular oxide island
phases_and_microstructures.material_state: exposed to S-CO2 at 700 °C (20 MPa) for 500 h

evidence.quote: while the nodular oxide regions on Alloy 718 are quite thicker (∼1.8 μm), these nodules exist as discontinuous islands
Alloy 625 is solid-solution strengthened, while Alloy 718 is precipitation-hardened mainly by γ″ [Ni3Nb].

evidence.quote: On the other hand, for Alloy 718, there is a slight reduction in UTS by 4% while there is hardly any change in elongation after S-CO2 exposure.

mechanisms.name: uphill diffusion of Nb
mechanisms.material_state: exposed to S-CO2 at 700 °C (20 MPa) for 500 h

evidence.quote: This phenomenon has been attributed to uphill diffusion of Nb to the surface due to decrease in Nb activity caused by Cr-depletion.

mechanisms.name: Boudouard reaction
mechanisms.material_state: exposed to S-CO2 at 700 °C (20 MPa) for 500 h

evidence.quote: This was attributed to the ingress of carbonaceous species such as CO2 or CO through the oxide layer to the oxide/metal interface, and subsequent deposition of C by the Boudouard reaction.

For Alloy 625, it is reported that prolonged exposures in temperatures ranging from 550–760 °C results in reduction of ductility [22–24]. This is attributed to the formation of γ″ and δ-phase in the matrix, which would have occurred after aging in 700 °C for 500 h.
